A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–I. Full-text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables and results.

before.justification: v2 reports original sampling experiments and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix G, molecular-conformation results in Appendix H, and biochemical sequence-design results in Appendix I.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including numerical outcomes in Tables 1–4 and 6–9 and sample visualisations in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithms 1–7 retain the same proposal/flow training, TB/SubTB losses, replay weighting and tempering. Equation (21)'s abbreviated parameter notation does not modify the network or sampling procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same gradient-free and gradient-based continuous targets, alanine-dipeptide conformations, and QM9, sEH, TFbind8 and L14-RNA1 tasks (Section 4; Appendices F, H and I).

E2.justification: The matched comparisons retain identical comparator rows, including diffusion/Monte Carlo baselines and replay-prioritisation alternatives. The background SMC citation replacement in Section 1 introduces no evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Metrics, evaluation sample sizes, end-of-training averaging procedures, model configurations and training budgets in Section 4 and Appendices F, H and I are unchanged.

E4.justification: The flow/interpolation and buffer ablations (Tables 3–4), training-loss analysis (Table 6), tempering and hyperparameter sensitivity studies (Figures 7–9), and sample visualisations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains mean and standard-deviation reporting over five runs; Appendix F.3 retains five random seeds. Figure 7's caption still specifies standard-deviation error bars from five runs.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–4 and 6–9, plotted results in Figures 2–10, and their reported findings are identical. No result entries, rankings or trends are added, removed or revised.

T1.justification: Definitions, assumptions and derivations are unchanged. Equation (21) changes NN_2^θ(t; θ) to NN_2^θ(t), preserving the same parameter dependence and mathematical meaning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution overview and Section 5 retain the same unification, off-policy training and empirical-performance claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mode coverage, weight degeneracy, training instability and loss bootstrapping are unchanged. The future-work discussion and molecular-sampling limitations are also retained.

D1.justification: The code-access statement and appendix implementation details remain unchanged, including architectures, hyperparameters, buffering, data processing and molecular MCMC settings. The Equation (21) edit supplies no new implementation information.

R1.justification: Section 1 replaces the SMC citation Halton (1962) with Gordon, Salmond and Smith (1993); the bibliography removes the former work and adds the latter. Appendix A and the broader research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits are limited to the citation/reference substitution, updated arXiv version/date stamp and removal of redundant parameter notation in Equation (21). The prose, section order and appendix organisation remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The replacement reference slightly reflows the bibliography's left column on page 11, and the shortened Equation (21) is recentered. Figures, tables, captions and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces one background citation and removes redundant notation in Equation (21). These limited editorial changes leave the scientific reasoning, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations unchanged, yielding no meaningful overall quality difference.
